# Active work — pixelkit

Live work, grouped by parent in `ROADMAP.md` order. Blocked work names its blocker inline.

## Unparented

### Accessibility through the App adapter, tested with real assistive technology

`proposed` · `@pixelkit.work.accessibility-validation/1`

Give App<S> the accessibility feature: own a Semantics, attach it with Ui::with_semantics every frame, publish the tree through PixelApp::accessibility_tree and route actions back through Input, so a Screen gets a screen-reader tree without implementing PixelApp. Then test, by hand, with Orca on Linux and VoiceOver on macOS: Tab and typed-focus transitions announce the right control, a modal dropdown hides the background controls, text fields report value and caret, and an action request on a button activates it. Record the findings as evidence with the AT version.

### Validate KMS, touch gestures and scroll physics on real Raspberry Pi hardware

`proposed` · `@pixelkit.work.hardware-validation/1`

Run the KMS host on at least two real panels (the official Pi touch display and an HDMI panel with a USB touch controller): mode set at the native and one non-native mode, all four rotations, two refresh rates, hotplug of the touch device, and a 24-hour soak for the missing-flip deadline. Run touch_tuning on a touchscreen, record sessions with touch_replay, and calibrate the GestureConfig and ScrollConfig defaults from those recordings. Each 'untested on hardware' label in the README and module docs is removed only by an evidence record citing the device, the kernel and the recording. Keep the recordings as regression fixtures.

### Reproducible performance comparison against egui and Freya on the same screen

`proposed` · `@pixelkit.work.performance-comparison/1`

Turn the reported ~30% memory reduction over Freya in Lege into a reproducible result. Build one operational screen (a table, a form, a scrolling list, a few controls) in liminalkit, egui and Freya in a separate benchmark workspace outside the published crates. Measure resident memory, startup latency, idle CPU (egui can also sleep, so measure rather than claim), p95 frame time under scripted interaction, binary size, and the same at 1080p, 1440p and 4K to find where software rendering's cost overtakes its memory savings. Report numbers with the machine, the resolution and the commit, and commit the harness so the table can be regenerated.

### Screenshots, an architecture guide, a tutorial, and crate-level API docs for outside readers

`proposed` · `@pixelkit.work.public-docs/1`

Add to the README a screenshot of a real Lege screen and of a kiosk screen on a Pi, and the gallery render. Write docs/ARCHITECTURE.md (the crates, the frame lifecycle, units, focus, the two hosts, the presenter seam) and a short tutorial that grows hello.rs into a form with a table and a dropdown. Give every crate a README and a lib.rs doc that answers what it is for and what it is not, written for someone who has not read the others. Make RUSTDOCFLAGS=-D warnings clean for the whole workspace (two broken links in liminalkit-raster png/ today) and keep it clean in CI.

### Packaging for a crates.io release, held until the owner decides the toolkit is ready

`proposed` · `@pixelkit.work.publish-packaging/1`

When and if publishing is decided: per-crate README, keywords and categories for the six component crates (the facade has them); cargo publish --dry-run for each in the order raster, text, shell, ui, windowing, kms, liminalkit; check the packaged file lists for test fixtures that should not ship (the Noto fonts behind test-fonts are the obvious one); a CHANGELOG; and a tag. The workspace already carries version requirements on its path dependencies and a description and repository on every crate.

### Measured exact SIMD coverage in raster kernels

`proposed` · `@pixelkit.work.raster-simd-coverage/1`

Keep coverage merging bit exact while adding SIMD only where profiles
justify it. The initial u8x32 path handles rows of at least 1024 bytes;
shorter glyph spans retain the scalar loop. Compare scalar and vector
medians for short and long rows on aarch64 and x86_64, then expand to
alpha coverage blending or opaque bitmap rows only after equivalent
output and a measured speed benefit. Preserve clipped tails and portable
behavior on unsupported targets.

### Font fallback across scripts, bidirectional text, and an optional mature shaper behind a feature

`proposed` · `@pixelkit.work.text-shaping-fallback/1`

Keep the dependency-free renderer as the default path and add what a general caller needs: per-run font fallback that walks a FontSet's chains by script and coverage rather than only by missing glyph; Unicode bidirectional reordering for mixed-direction lines; and an optional `shaper-rustybuzz` (or equivalent) feature that routes shaping through a full OpenType engine while liminalkit-text keeps rasterization, caching and wrapping. The feature must be off by default and must not change output for the bundled Latin and Thai fonts when off. Measure the binary-size and startup cost of the feature so an appliance build can refuse it knowingly.

### Dialogs, menus, overlays, drag-and-drop and multi-line text, as caller-owned state

`proposed` · `@pixelkit.work.ui-capabilities/1`

Add the capabilities an operational application reaches for next, each in the shape Dropdown already has: a value the screen owns, an input prepass that claims clicks and keys before the background draws, and a draw call that runs last. A modal dialog (scrim, focus trapped inside, Escape and a result enum); a context menu and a menu bar sharing the popup machinery; a generic overlay/popover anchored to a rect; in-app drag-and-drop between lists with a caller-owned DragState (OS file drops already arrive through on_file_drop); a multi-line text field with wrapping, vertical scrolling and the same grapheme-boundary editing as the single-line one. Every one of these must state in its signature what it owns and what persists between frames.
